title: When the tab has no room left, the worker gets a new tab instead of an unusable sliver
action: hps-12 put the width guard on the PARENT pane (refuse under 60 columns). The live acceptance probe shows that is the wrong side of the split, and that a refusal alone kills fan-out anyway. Measured, tab root 120x43, three concurrent runs: the first split produced a 60-column child and that run completed end to end with its ack and result files; the other two got 30-column children and BOTH died with herdr's `agent_prompt_stalled` — `agent prompt produced no observed state change within 5000 ms; status is idle`. agy renders its banner fine at 30 columns but never takes the submitted pointer there, so the symptom is a stalled submission, not a visibly broken TUI. Three changes. (1) MOVE THE GUARD TO THE CHILD. What must be usable is the pane the agent gets, so the rule is that a parent may only be split when the RESULTING child would still be at least the minimum wide — with `--ratio 0.5` that means the parent needs twice the minimum. Set the minimum from measurement, not taste, and state the evidence in the doc comment: 60 columns carried a full agy round to a written result; 30 columns stalled every submission; the boundary between them is unmeasured, so the minimum takes the last known-good value rather than a guess in the gap. (2) NEW TAB INSTEAD OF A SLIVER. When no pane in the caller's tab can yield a usable child, do NOT refuse — ask herdr for a fresh tab and give the worker its root pane directly, with no split at all, so it starts at full width. A live capture of `herdr tab create --workspace w4 --cwd <path> --label bee-probe`, trimmed: `{"id":"cli:tab:create","result":{"root_pane":{"pane_id":"w4:p31","cwd":"<path>","tab_id":"w4:tE","workspace_id":"w4"},"tab":{...}}}` — the pane id is at `result.root_pane.pane_id`. Add it to the `Herdr` trait beside `pane_split`, with `RealHerdr`, `FakeHerdr` and `PanicHerdr` impls, pass the workspace the caller's own pane reports, the run's `--cwd`, and a label naming the job, and do NOT pass `--focus`: a worker must never steal the human's focus, exactly as `pane_split` already passes `--no-focus`. Pin the parse with a test over the captured body above, no process. (3) REFUSE ONLY AS THE LAST RESORT. If the tab cannot be created either, keep hps-12's typed refusal — naming the widths, the minimum and the remedy — but add that a new tab was attempted and why it failed. An unreadable layout still falls open to the caller's own pane and never refuses, unchanged. Tests: a roomy tab still splitting in place; a tab with no usable candidate creating a tab and using its root pane with no split call; the pane id parsed from the captured create body; a failed create producing the refusal that mentions both attempts; and an unreadable layout still falling back to the caller's own pane.

truths: The width guard is on the resulting child pane, not the parent
A tab with no room left yields a fresh tab's root pane, unsplit and unfocused, instead of a sliver or a refusal
The minimum's doc comment cites the measured 60-works / 30-stalls evidence and says the boundary between them is unmeasured
A refusal happens only when the new tab could not be created, and says both attempts failed
